1	# DRIVER_GUIDE.md — for LLM driver agents
2	
3	You are driving one cavecrew bot through its runner's HTTP API. The runner
4	(`cave/runner.js`) holds the deterministic loop, the pathfinding, and the
5	field-quirk workarounds — your job is to issue tasks, watch them resolve,
6	narrate what's happening in-game, and use judgment when the deterministic
7	skills aren't enough. Check `CIV.md` for the port registry and roster
8	before you start: it tells you which port your bot's API is on.
9	
10	All examples below use `curl.exe` from Windows PowerShell (the `.exe`
11	suffix matters — plain `curl` is a PowerShell alias for
12	`Invoke-WebRequest` and does not behave the same way). Replace `3201`
13	with your bot's actual port from `CIV.md`.
14	
15	## Poll discipline — read this first
16	
17	- **Single-poll contract**: every task response from `/status` carries
18	  its own state and result. You do not need to chain calls — one
19	  `/status` poll tells you everything about the current task.
20	- **Poll every 15-30 seconds** while a task is running. Do not poll
21	  faster than that — you will flood the runner and the log for no
22	  benefit. A `chop` or `mine` task can legitimately take a couple of
23	  minutes.
24	- **One task at a time.** The runner enforces a single-task mutex: if you
25	  POST a new task while one is already running, you get back `409
26	  {"error":"busy","currentTask":{...}}`. Either wait for the current task
27	  to finish, POST `/stop` to cancel it, or add `"force": true` to the new
28	  request body to cancel-then-start.
29	- Never spam-loop `/eval` or `/status`. If you're unsure what's
30	  happening, one `/status` call answers it.
31	
32	## Escalation rule
33	
34	If a deterministic skill (`/chop`, `/mine`, `/goto`, etc.) **fails twice
35	in a row on the same objective**, stop retrying it as-is. Instead:
36	
37	1. Drop to `/eval` and reason through the problem manually (see below).
38	2. **Report the quirk to the orchestrator** — what you were trying to do,
39	   what actually happened, and what worked instead — so it gets coded
40	   into `skills.js` as a permanent fix. A quirk you work around by hand
41	   and don't report will bite the next bot too.
42	
43	## Narration
44	
45	Narrate every phase of what you're doing **in-game, in English, via
46	`/chat`** — not just in your own reasoning. Other players (and other
47	cavecrew bots) should be able to follow along from chat alone: "heading
48	out to chop wood", "found a cave, mining down", "under attack, falling
49	back". Keep lines short.
50	
51	## Conduct rules
52	
53	- **Never attack players.** `/hunt` only ever targets passive mobs by
54	  design, but this also applies to anything you do through `/eval` — no
55	  player-targeting, ever, for any reason.
56	- **Never touch the other tribe's chests or builds.** The other tribe on
57	  this server is **FurzFriedrich, MettMarcel, BuddelBernd, KackboonKevin**.
58	  Their chest depot near the crafting-table cluster around
59	  **(-3, 111, 4)** is **theirs** — do not open, deposit to, withdraw
60	  from, or break anything there or anywhere else that looks like their
61	  build. When in doubt, back off and ask in chat rather than guess.
62	- **Never leave drops on the ground.** Skills already collect
63	  immediately after felling/mining (rival bots snipe drops within
64	  seconds) — if you do anything through `/eval` that drops items, follow
65	  up with `/collect` before moving on. **Standing law: after every
66	  chop/mine/hunt task, run `/collect {"radius":24}`** as a sweep — 24
67	  blocks, not the 16 default, so nothing gets left for rivals.
68	- **Protected blocks — never dug by skills.** `safeDig` (the one
69	  choke point every `/chop`, `/mine`, `/staircase`, `/branchmine`, etc.
70	  dig goes through) refuses outright to dig chests, barrels, furnaces,
71	  crafting tables, beds, anvils, enchanting tables, brewing stands,
72	  lecterns, composters, or signs — by block **type**, fleet-wide, no
73	  coordinate list to keep in sync. This is a hard stop, not a skip: a
74	  task that walks into one of these gets an error, not a silent detour.
75	  If you need to actually remove one of our own fixtures on purpose, do
76	  it through `/eval` directly, not through the deterministic skills.
77	- **Wedge-detection.** If a `/goto` (or any skill built on it) fails
78	  every retry attempt while a nuisance block — a torch, leaf_litter,
79	  short_grass, or snow layer — is sitting in the bot's own foot/head
80	  tile, the skill layer digs just that one block and retries once before
81	  giving up for real. Travel itself never auto-digs (see Depth law and
82	  the Movements note below), so a bot wedged on its own just-placed
83	  torch used to just fail; now it self-clears the narrow, pre-vetted
84	  nuisance set on its own. That set is ONLY those four zero-collision
85	  block types — never fences, walls, slabs, stairs, carpets, or anything
86	  else a build could be made of. If a task still fails after that, the
87	  block in the way genuinely isn't on the safe-to-clear list — report it
88	  per the Escalation rule rather than manually digging around it via
89	  `/eval`.
90	- **Best tool always equipped.** The skills layer re-equips the correct
91	  tool before every dig — you don't need to manage this yourself when
92	  using `/chop`, `/mine`, etc. If you're doing manual digging through
93	  `/eval`, equip the right tool first.
94	- **Idle & nag law (two-tier).** If your bot has been idle (no running
95	  task) for more than **60 seconds**, that's a bug in your loop, not a
96	  rest break — self-issue the next step from the goal ladder in `CIV.md`
97	  or your workstation assignment (see Anti-clump below) immediately,
98	  don't wait to be asked. Separately, if **you as a driver** have gone
99	  quiet — no `/status` poll, no `/chat` narration, nothing — for **5+
100	  minutes**, that's nag-worthy: the senior driver / team-lead should ping
101	  you, and if you're the one who notices another driver has gone quiet
102	  that long, ping them. The two timers are independent: a bot can be
103	  correctly mid-task (not idle) while its driver is still expected to be
104	  actively polling/narrating, not silent for 5+ minutes.
105	- **Anti-clump — per-bot workstations.** Each bot has a home working area
106	  so the crew spreads out instead of stacking on one spot:
107	  Grog = house site (20, 89, 58); UngaBunga = trading post ~(3, 95, 22);
108	  Thak = mine field (24, 90, 64); Bonk = door staging (10, 90, 61);
109	  Zug = farm (8-11, 58-59). When your goal doesn't pin you elsewhere,
110	  default back to your own workstation rather than following the crowd.
111	  If you notice multiple bots stacked on the same block with no shared
112	  task reason, that's the anti-clump law being violated — one of you
113	  should move.
114	- **Watching ≠ working.** Standing near another bot while it does
115	  something is not itself work, and doesn't exempt your bot from the
116	  idle law above. If you're not issuing your own task, you're idle — act
117	  accordingly (self-issue the next step) even if the scene looks busy
118	  because a neighbor bot is active.
119	- **Ground-truth verify.** Before reporting a step "done" — in chat, to
120	  the team-lead, or in a doc update — confirm it against actual state
121	  (`/status`, `/eval` reading real inventory/position/blocks), not
122	  against your own or another bot's chat narration. Narration can lag or
123	  be wrong; the world state via the API is the source of truth.
124	- **Equality doctrine.** All five bots are equally cavecrew. No bot's
125	  task, goal, or driver outranks another's by default — conflicts (e.g.
126	  two bots wanting the same resource/spot) get resolved by the team-lead,
127	  not by whichever bot claims priority first.
128	- **Depth law — SOLVED.** `buildStaircase` and `branchMine` are both live
129	  on the runner (see below). Deep ore goes through that pair only. Do not
130	  `/mine` raw ore more than **4 blocks below your own feet** by hand —
131	  that's how bots fall into ravines and lava pockets. Staircase down
132	  properly first.
133	- **Trade etiquette.** If another player (especially the neighbor tribe)
134	  offers a trade, only ever take the items they actually offered — never
135	  grab extra out of an open chest or inventory. Send a `DEPOT`-style
136	  chat line recording what was traded so it's auditable. Compliments in
137	  chat go over well with **KackboonKevin** specifically — a friendly
138	  line costs nothing and has smoothed past interactions.
139	- **Trading post protocol.** Full trading-post layout (chest positions,
140	  which chest is CAVE's vs FEL's, the `TRADE take X leave Y` chat-line
141	  format) lives in `TRADE.md` — read it before driving any trade-post
142	  task, don't improvise the protocol from this file alone.
143	- **tp-rescue policy — SUPERSEDED.** Orchestrator/RCON `/tp` rescues are
144	  now **BANNED**. See "HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)" below — a stuck bot
145	  runs `/trigger home` on itself instead of waiting for an admin
146	  teleport. `/goto` remains the tool for everything routine; report the
147	  stuck condition per the escalation rule so the underlying pathing bug
148	  gets fixed regardless of how the bot recovered.
149	- **Blink protocol.** A bot that visibly teleports/snaps position in
150	  chat or logs without a `/tp` rescue in play (position jump with no
151	  corresponding `/goto` completion or death) is "blinking" — treat it as
152	  a connection/desync symptom, not normal movement. Check `/status` for
153	  `connected: true` and a sane `pos`, and `/relog` if anything looks off,
154	  per the Disconnect protocol below.
155	- **Plugin-first doctrine.** Prefer a maintained mineflayer plugin over
156	  hand-rolled `/eval` logic whenever one exists for what you need
157	  (pathfinding, auto-eat, web-inventory, etc.) — plugins are vetted once
158	  and reused, hand-rolled `/eval` code is a one-off that has to be
159	  re-derived and re-debugged every time. Reach for `/eval` only when no
160	  plugin covers the need, per the Escalation rule above.
161	- **Build standards.** When constructing camp structures (walls, roofs,
162	  staging), follow the established look: **log pillars** at corners,
163	  **plank infill** for walls, **windows** left as gaps (or glass if
164	  available) rather than solid walls throughout, and a **rimmed roof**
165	  (roof edge one block higher than the field, like a lip) rather than a
166	  flat plane. Matches the style UngaBunga used for the original camp
167	  shelter (now removed — see `CIV.md` state refresh — but the standard
168	  still applies to any rebuild).
169	- **Signs-for-labeling law.** Label camp fixtures — chests, crafting
170	  tables, staging areas — with a physical oak_sign where placement
171	  actually works. Where sign placement fails (see the sign-on-chest
172	  quirk logged in `CIV.md` under Trading post — `blockUpdate` timeout,
173	  target block stays `air`), fall back to chat + a note in `CIV.md`/
174	  `TRADE.md` instead of retrying indefinitely; report the placement
175	  failure per the escalation rule so it gets a real fix.
176	- **Chat tiers (real talk vs everything else) — now auto-classified.** The
177	  default `/chat` style (`"talk"`, or no `style` at all) routes through the
178	  runner's `smartChat`: a line starting with `!` is stripped of the `!` and
179	  sent as **important white** real chat — an announcement worth every
180	  bot/player noticing; everything else (routine narration AND every
181	  protocol/ledger line — `DEPOT `, `TRADE `, `USING `, `FREE `,
182	  `LEASE-BREAK `, `BASE `, `CLAIM `, `HELLO `, `OFFER `) becomes **grey**
183	  narration routed to the Discord status feed, never public game chat. You
184	  don't need to pick a style for ordinary narration ("heading out to chop
185	  wood") or for a DEPOT/protocol ledger line — just `/chat` it and the
186	  classification happens for you. Use `"style":"status"` to force grey
187	  regardless of content, or `"style":"rainbow"` for a genuine tribe-wide
188	  proclamation (a goal-ladder milestone, a new pact) — those still go out as
189	  real chat, deliberately, since you asked for it by name.
190	- **TOTAL DE-CHAT (chief, 2026-09-01) — game chat is real talk only, full
191	  stop.** Every protocol-ledger prefix above (`TRADE `/`USING `/`FREE `/
192	  `LEASE-BREAK `/`BASE `/`CLAIM `/`HELLO `/`OFFER `) used to go out as real
193	  white chat, verbatim, because other tribes parsed public chat for those
194	  exact prefixes — that stopped being true once inter-tribe coordination
195	  moved to the claims registry + repo/Discord
196	  ([monkeorg/cavecrew-mcp#1](https://github.com/monkeorg/cavecrew-mcp/issues/1)).
197	  This supersedes the earlier "ledger lines must stay REAL white chat" law
198	  and generalizes the DEPOT de-chat decree below to every prefix, not just
199	  DEPOT. Nothing changes for you as a driver — keep sending every ledger
200	  line through `/chat` exactly as documented, unchanged format; only the
201	  destination moved, same as DEPOT already did.
202	
203	## DEPOT ledger
204	
205	Once cavecrew has its own chests (goal ladder step 6 in `CIV.md`), every
206	deposit or withdrawal against a cavecrew chest gets a ledger line so the
207	whole tribe can follow the ledger.
208	
209	> **2026-09-01 (chief):** these lines go to the **Discord status feed**, not
210	> public white chat — see TOTAL DE-CHAT under Chat tiers above, which now
211	> covers every protocol/ledger prefix, not just DEPOT. You still send them
212	> the same way (`/chat`, format unchanged); the runner classifies and routes
213	> them.
214	
215	```
216	DEPOT +N item (chest X)
217	DEPOT -N item (chest X)
218	```
219	
220	`N` is the count, `item` the item name, `X` identifies which chest (a
221	short label or coordinate). Example:
222	
223	```
224	DEPOT +64 cobblestone (chest A)
225	DEPOT -8 iron_ingot (chest A)
226	```
227	
228	Send this line via `/chat` yourself right after a `/deposit` or
229	`/withdraw` call succeeds.
230	
231	## Panic reflex (automatic)
232	
233	The runner watches health at game-packet speed, not driver-poll speed:
234	if health drops below **8**, it fires automatically — no `/chat` or
235	`/stop` from you required. It aborts the current task, announces
236	`!HP <n>/20 - breaking off, reacting to danger!` (real white chat), and
237	then either **flees to camp** (if reasonably close and shallow) or
238	**seals itself in place and eats** (if far from camp or deep below it —
239	a blind flee across unknown terrain is riskier than holing up). This is
240	debounced 30s so it won't refire on every low-health tick. Check
241	`/events` for a `panic` entry and `/status` afterward — the panic
242	response runs as a normal task (`kind: "panic-response"`), so it shows
243	up like anything else. Treat a panic firing as a real incident worth a
244	`/status` check and a chat narration of what you find, same as any other
245	unexpected task failure.
246	
247	## Death protocol
248	
249	- A death **aborts the current task** — whatever was running is over,
250	  don't assume it resumes on respawn.
251	- `GET /status` carries a `deathCount` field. Check it after any
252	  unexpected task failure or gap in `/events` — a jump means the bot
253	  died and respawned since you last looked.
254	- After a death, if the bot lost its kit (tools/armor), run a `/recover`
255	  kit run: get back to camp/depot, `ensureTool` (see below) the essentials
256	  back into hand, and only then resume the goal you were on.
257	- Poisoned targets (mobs/blocks flagged poisonous by the runner) are
258	  **auto-skipped** by the skills layer — you don't need to detect these
259	  yourself, but don't fight the skip by manually targeting them through
260	  `/eval`.
261	
262	## Disconnect protocol
263	
264	- If the bot has dropped off the server, endpoints return **503** while
265	  it's offline — that's the signal, not a bug to route around.
266	- First aid: `POST /relog` (reconnects the bot). Try this before
267	  anything else.
268	- If `/relog` doesn't bring it back and you hit a **second** disconnect
269	  in the same session, **report it** to the team-lead rather than
270	  looping `/relog` indefinitely — two disconnects in a row usually means
271	  something upstream (server restart, kick, crash) that a driver can't
272	  fix alone.
273	
274	## Structured mining (buildStaircase → branchMine)
275	
276	This pair of skills is **live on the runner** — the depth law is solved.
277	This is the required pattern for any real ore run.
278	
279	1. `POST /buildStaircase` to descend safely to target depth (torches +
280	   safe steps, not a raw dig-down).
281	2. `POST /branchMine` from the bottom of the staircase to sweep ore
282	   bands at that depth (branches off a central shaft, standard
283	   strip-mining pattern).
284	3. Only fall back to plain `/mine` for shallow, surface-adjacent blocks
285	   — not for anything past the 4-block depth law above.
286	
287	Exact body shapes for `/buildStaircase` and `/branchMine` — check
288	`/status` or ask the team-lead if the runner's response shape isn't
289	obvious from a first call; document what you learn back to `CIV.md` or
290	`skills.js` per the escalation rule.
291	
292	## ensureTool (auto tool chain)
293	
294	Skills that need a specific tool call `ensureTool` internally. When your
295	bot's inventory doesn't have the right tool:
296	
297	1. It checks current inventory first — no wasted trip if you already
298	   have it.
299	2. If missing, it goes to the depot at **(11, 89, 55)** and withdraws
300	   the tool if the chest has one — sends the `DEPOT -N item (chest X)`
301	   ledger line for you.
302	3. If the depot doesn't have it either, it walks the **craft chain**:
303	   gather/withdraw materials → craft table if needed → craft the tool.
304	
305	You don't need to drive this by hand — it's automatic inside `/chop`,
306	`/mine`, `/buildStaircase`, `/branchMine`, etc. Just expect a task to
307	take longer than usual the first time a bot needs a new tool tier.
308	
309	## placeBlock — slow confirm
310	
311	`placeBlock` (used internally by staircase/shelter skills, and via
312	`/eval` if you call it directly) confirms placement **slowly** — the
313	runner waits for the block-update packet before considering it done
314	rather than assuming success the instant the packet is sent. Don't treat
315	a pause here as a hang; give it a few extra seconds before you decide
316	something's wrong and escalate.
317	
318	## Team tags
319	
320	Each bot is on its own colored in-game team, named `cave_<name>` (e.g.
321	`cave_Grog`, `cave_UngaBunga`, `cave_Zug`), with chat prefixed `[CAVE]`
322	so tribe members are visually distinguishable from the neighbor tribe at
323	a glance. When a **new bot** joins the roster, it needs its team created
324	and joined via RCON before it's doing real work:
325	
326	```powershell
327	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team add cave_<Name>"
328	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team join cave_<Name> <Name>"
329	```
330	
331	Run these from `C:\Users\phili\tools\minecraft-mcp-v2`. Add the new
332	bot's name and port to the roster table in `CIV.md` at the same time.
333	
334	## Engine choice on `/goto`
335	
336	`engine` on `/goto` currently defaults to the runner's own pick (see
337	`GET /status`'s `"engine"` field) but you can force it: `"pf"`
338	(pathfinder) or `"ash"` (ashfinder). As of now, **`pf` is measured
339	faster on open ground** — prefer it for camp-to-camp or surface travel.
340	`ash` remains an option worth trying for tight cave/underground
341	navigation where pathfinder struggles. A proper safety A/B between the
342	two engines is **pending** — don't treat either as fully vetted yet, and
343	report any stuck/unsafe pathing back per the escalation rule regardless
344	of which engine you used.
345	
346	## API reference
347	
348	Base URL for every endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — bind is
349	loopback-only, this is not reachable off the machine.
350	
351	### `GET /status`
352	
353	Poll this to check on the current (or last) task and vitals.
354	
355	```powershell
356	curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:3201/status
357	```
358	
359	Response shape:
360	
361	```json
362	{
363	  "name": "UngaBunga",
364	  "connected": true,
365	  "pos": { "x": 12.5, "y": 64, "z": -8.1 },
366	  "health": 20,
367	  "food": 18,
368	  "gamemode": "survival",
369	  "inventory": [{ "name": "oak_log", "count": 6 }],
370	  "currentTask": {
371	    "id": "task-17",
372	    "kind": "chop",
373	    "state": "running",
374	    "detail": "chopping tree 3/8",
375	    "result": null
376	  },
377	  "lastError": null,
378	  "engine": "auto"
379	}
380	```
381	
382	`currentTask.state` is one of `running`, `done`, `failed`. `result`
383	carries the task's return value once it's `done`, or a failure summary
384	once `failed`.
385	
386	### `POST /goto`
387	
388	Looping goto — re-issues the pathfinder goal internally up to 5 times on
389	timeout before giving up. You don't need to retry this yourself.
390	
391	```powershell
392	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/goto `
393	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
394	  -d '{"x":100,"y":64,"z":-40,"range":1,"timeoutMs":45000}'
395	```
396	
397	Body: `{x, y, z, range?=1, timeoutMs?=45000, engine?}`. `engine` is
398	optional — `"auto"` (tries ashfinder, falls back to pathfinder), `"ash"`
399	(ashfinder only), or `"pf"` (pathfinder only). Omit it to use the runner's

556	## HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)
557	
558	A server-side datapack (`cavehome`, installed in the world's
559	`datapacks/` folder — not part of this repo) gives every player two
560	legit `/trigger` commands, no admin involvement needed:
561	
562	- `/trigger sethome` — saves the runner's current position as *their
563	  own* home. Per-player automatically (scoreboard-backed, keyed by
564	  username — 8+ bots sharing the server each get their own home, no
565	  collision).
566	- `/trigger home` — teleports the runner back to their saved home. If
567	  no home was ever set, it sends a grey hint instead of erroring:
568	  `[cavehome] no home set yet - run /trigger sethome first.`
569	
570	Drive it exactly like any other chat command, through `/eval` (not
571	`/chat`, since `/trigger` is a raw slash-command, not a talk line):
572	
573	```powershell
574	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
575	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
576	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger sethome\")"}'
577	```
578	
579	```powershell
580	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
581	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
582	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger home\")"}'
583	```
584	
585	**Doctrine:**
586	
587	1. **Set home at the camp yard** — around **(12, 93, 50)** — on spawn
588	   and whenever you're back at camp for a while. A stale home (deep in
589	   a mine you've since left) is still safer to return to than nowhere,
590	   but refresh it when you can.
591	2. **Try the FEEDBACK.md stuck-taxonomy self-rescues first** — the
592	   wedge-detection nuisance-block clear, a `/stop` + re-`/goto`, digging
593	   out by hand via `/eval`. `/trigger home` is the **escalation**, not
594	   the first move, for a bot that's step-snagged, full-wedged, or sealed
595	   in a pocket it can't path or dig out of in reasonable time.
596	3. **This replaces orchestrator/RCON teleports**, which are now BANNED
597	   (see the superseded tp-rescue policy above) — the bot rescues
598	   *itself* with a command any regular player can run, not an admin
599	   backdoor.
600	4. Still narrate it in chat and report the stuck condition per the
601	   Escalation rule — `/trigger home` gets you out, it doesn't excuse
602	   skipping the report that gets the underlying pathing bug fixed.
603

606	`(24.66, 103.42, 131.70)`, `/trigger home` returned it to

1020	## [shipped] ROOT CAUSE (self-correction): my own "chest has only 12 oak_log / 15 torch" reads were a single-stack read bug, not a real drain — Grog, 2026-09-01 10:15
1021	Reported chest A oak_log at 12 and chest B torch at 15 mid-lamp-mission (see the DEPOT -8/-4 lines
1022	and my Phase B report). Team-lead's audit.mjs snapshot came back with the REAL totals: oak_log 76,
1023	torch 80 — no drain, my reads were just wrong. Root cause, found by re-reading my own eval code:
1024	every "how much of item X does this chest/inventory hold" check I did this whole session used the
1025	pattern `containerItems().find(i=>i.name===X)` (or `bot.inventory.items().find(...)`) then reported
1026	`.count` off that ONE match. `.find()` returns only the FIRST matching stack — if the item is split
1027	across multiple stacks in the container (very likely for bulk materials that exceed 64, or that
1028	just got deposited/withdrawn piecemeal by several bots), `.count` silently reports that one stack's
1029	size, not the item's real total. The actual `c.withdraw(type, null, N)` calls I made were NOT
1030	affected by this (mineflayer's withdraw pulls N units across however many matching stacks exist,
1031	confirmed correct both times — my inventory after each withdraw had exactly the requested amount),
1032	so no materials were actually lost or misdelivered; only my SELF-REPORTED "had:" diagnostic numbers
1033	in chat/reports were wrong, and I compounded it by reporting those numbers as if they were the
1034	chest's total instead of one stack's size.
1035	
1036	Fix for any driver reading a chest/inventory count for reporting (not just to identify an item
1037	exists): sum ALL matching stacks, not just the first —
1038	`containerItems().filter(i=>i.name===X).reduce((s,i)=>s+i.count,0)`. The runner's own `/status`
1039	inventory list already does this correctly (confirmed earlier this session: it showed
1040	`iron_pickaxe: count 2` correctly after two separate 1-count tool stacks existed) — trust `/status`
1041	or a summed reduce, never a bare `.find(...).count`, when the number itself matters. Marking
1042	[shipped] since this is now understood and the fix is just "read chests correctly next time," not
1043	a code change — but flagging loudly since I personally used the broken pattern many times this
1044	session for other chest reads too (not just these two), so any of my earlier "chest X holds Y"
1045	numbers in this log or in BASE.md should be treated as possibly a single-stack undercount rather
1046	than gospel until re-verified by audit.mjs.

input.description: Thak branchmine progress + y-drop watch
input.command:
baseline=53.7
prev_trunk=""
while true; do
  json=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3205/status)
  state=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['currentTask']['state'] if d.get('currentTask') else 'none')")
  detail=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['currentTask'].get('detail') if d.get('currentTask') else '')")
  y=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['pos']['y'])")
  if [ "$detail" != "$prev_trunk" ]; then
    echo "PROGRESS detail=$detail y=$y state=$state"
    prev_trunk="$detail"
  fi
  drop=$(python3 -c "print(1 if ($baseline - $y) > 2 else 0)")
  if [ "$drop" = "1" ]; then
    echo "ALERT y-drop >2: baseline=$baseline now=$y detail=$detail"
    baseline=$y
  fi
  if [ "$state" = "done" ] || [ "$state" = "failed" ]; then
    echo "TERMINAL state=$state detail=$detail y=$y"
    echo "$json" > /tmp/thak_branchmine_final.json
    break
  fi
  sleep 15
done

## [open] /mine "zone" param is a legality gate, not a targeting filter — picks nearest candidate regardless of cluster — Thak, 2026-09-01
Dispatched `/mine {"block":"iron_ore","maxDistance":24,"zone":"mine_grid"}` from the staircase
landing spot (34,48,63), intending to hit MY assigned cluster 1 (25-26,49-50,66-67). Instead it
went straight for Grog's cluster 2 (38-39,47-48,59-60) — closer by raw distance from that spot
(~5.7 vs ~9.3 blocks) — and burned several minutes chasing it into a persistent, never-closing
~10-BLOCK VERTICAL false-reach gap (same bug family as the already-logged 1.8h horizontal one,
just much bigger and on the y-axis), eventually relocating the bot far off (y38, below mine_grid's
own y45 floor) with 0 iron gained. Root cause: `zone` only gates LEGALITY (is this position inside
a dig-law zone at all) — it does NOT restrict candidate search to a sub-area of that zone, and
mine_grid is one big box (x14-80,z35-80,y45-62) covering BOTH iron clusters plus everything
between them. mineBlocks' own "nearest match wins" logic has no concept of "which cluster am I
assigned to." Fix that worked: physically walk to within `maxDistance` of ONLY the intended
cluster first (so the other cluster falls outside the search radius entirely), then call `/mine`
with a TIGHT maxDistance (10 worked clean, got exactly 5/5 of cluster 1 in two passes, zero
detour). Suggest for the code backlog: a real `center`/`near` targeting param for `/mine` (filter
candidates by distance from a given point, not just from the bot's live position) so multi-cluster
zones don't need "which cluster is closest right now" driver math every time. Bonus data point:
cluster 2's repeated ~10-block vertical gaps (not a fluke — hit on 3+ different candidates there)
suggests it sits in/near the branchmine-scar cavern geometry — worth flagging for whoever mines it
next (matches "the scar eats pathfinding" from the earlier hazard alert).

## [open] genuinely undug rock corridor near cluster 3 → mineBlocks/buildStaircase both false-reach loop instead of digging through → real drowning incident — Thak, 2026-09-01
Cluster 3 (23-24,y46-47,77-79) sits 4-5 blocks past a wall of SOLID, NEVER-DUG stone from the
nearest reachable position — ground-truth blockAt scan confirmed z74-76 at x24,y45-49 were 100%
stone, no existing tunnel/cavity at all, not degraded terrain. Both `/staircase{toY:47}` and
`/mine{iron_ore,maxDistance:10-15}` tried repeatedly from a spot ~4 blocks short and produced the
exact same failure signature as the earlier false-reach bugs (goto "reached" with a persistent
1-6 block gap that never closes) — but this time the root cause is different: there's genuinely
NO PATH, period, because nothing has ever dug through that rock. Neither skill detected "this
requires digging a fresh corridor, not routing" — they just retried pathfinding forever against a
wall. Escalation-rule fix that worked: manual /eval `bot.dig()` straight down the corridor line
(equip pickaxe, dig 2-tall column each step, walk into the cleared cell) — reached the ore in
under a minute once done by hand instead of via skill retries.

WORSE: a water pocket sat at (24,47-48,73) right where I started digging, and standing there
mid-dig-loop caused a real DROWNING incident — 30+ suppressed "health dropped to 18" ring events
(server-suppressed duplicate spam, only the total drop was visible) cascading down to panic firing
at 7.67hp (`panic reflex firing`, health event 444). Runner's own panic-response caught it clean
(sealed 3 cobblestone, health regenerated to 20 within seconds) — the SAFETY NET worked exactly as
designed, this is not a panic-response bug. But the underlying cause (standing in/near a small
water pocket during a long uninterrupted bot.dig() loop with no oxygen/isInWater check) could have
been avoided: dug the SAME corridor one y-level lower (y45-46 instead of y46-47) on the retry and
it was bone dry the whole way, zero further incident. Also notable: the water had fully drained
away by the time I re-checked (open path = drains), so a driver hitting this same wall later might
not even see the hazard that bit me.

Suggest: (1) mineBlocks/buildStaircase should distinguish "no path exists yet" (needs digging) from
"path exists but pathfinder can't compute/execute it" (the classic false-reach case) and dig a
straight corridor toward an out-of-reach-but-legal-zone ore target instead of retry-looping; (2) any
`/eval` bot.dig() loop that runs more than a couple seconds should check `bot.entity.isInWater` /
`bot.oxygenLevel` between steps and bail/surface if either goes bad, rather than trusting the panic
reflex as the only safety net; (3) worth an isInWater/oxygenLevel check added to the generic
runTargetWithWatchdog used by staircase/branchmine/mineBlocks too, same reasoning.

296	
297	Research pass (gh CLI, no installs/launches) into the two blockers hit trying
298	to bring PATH 1 up on HMC 2.10.0 / MC 1.21.11: (1) `-lwjgl` render patch hangs
299	forever pre-title-screen after spamming "Found unknown and unsupported uniform

303	### Blocker 1 — `-lwjgl` render hang on blur uniforms
304	
305	Root cause, near-certain: the exact string "Found unknown and unsupported
306	uniform" is **vanilla Mojang code**, not a headlessmc string — confirmed by
307	grepping public 1.21.11 decompile mirrors, it lives in
308	`com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlProgram`. On a real GPU this line is a harmless,
309	non-fatal WARN. The hang is a HeadlessMc-side consequence: `-lwjgl` works by
310	bytecode-redirecting LWJGL/GL calls to fake return values instead of talking
311	to a real GPU (`headlessmc-lwjgl/.../redirections/LwjglRedirections.java`),
312	and that emulation layer is incomplete for the newer RenderPipeline/GPU-device
313	abstraction Mojang shipped around 1.21.9-1.21.11 and is still shipping today
314	(Mojang has since moved to calendar version numbers — 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.2 all
315	come chronologically *after* 1.21.11 in this same codebase's version list).
316	
317	Evidence the maintainers are actively chasing this exact surface, release by
318	release:
319	- **2.9.0** (2026-04-04): [PR #407](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/407)
320	  "fix(1.21.11): Fix crash" — fixed `MemoryUtil;memSlice`, which had literally
321	  been stubbed to always `return null` ("TODO... null is fairly safe rn"),
322	  causing the 1.21.11 boot NPE in
323	  [issue #388](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/388).
324	  Sibling [PR #406](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/406) fixed
325	  the same-shaped 1.21.10 crash,
326	  [issue #389](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/389).
327	- **2.10.0** (2026-07-13): [PR #426](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/426)
328	  "fix(26.2): Fixed lwjgl headless launching for 26.2" — fixed `DeviceLimits`/
329	  `GPUDevices` emulation gaps for the version right after 1.21.11.
330	- 1.21.11's own build support was gated on
331	  [headlesshq/mc-runtime-test#116](https://github.com/headlesshq/mc-runtime-test/issues/116)
332	  (unimined tooling), closed 2026-04-04 — separate from the runtime bugs above.
333	- No release newer than 2.10.0 exists; commits on `main` since the 2.10.0 tag
334	  are chore-only (logo, CI) — nothing queued that would fix this.
335	- Exhaustive search (issues/PRs/commits/discussions/code-search, org-wide) for
336	  "blur" or "uniform" turns up **nothing** else — the only unrelated hit is
337	  `hmc.lwjgl.uniformoffsetalignment` (`GL_UNIFORM_BUFFER_OFFSET_ALIGNMENT`,
338	  a buffer-alignment constant, not the blur pipeline's uniform names). **This
339	  exact hang is unreported upstream as of 2.10.0 / today.**
340	- No LwjglProperties flag exists to selectively skip RenderPipeline/uniform
341	  validation while staying in `-lwjgl` mode. `hmc.lwjgl.ignore.classes`
342	  exists but excluding a class from redirection while headless just crashes

345	**Workaround that should fix it today: stop using `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's
346	own README says outright: "You can also achieve headless mode without
347	patching lwjgl by running headlessmc with a virtual framebuffer like Xvfb."

377	### Blocker 2 — JLine console over a plain pipe (no TTY)
378	
379	Confirmed root cause + confirmed fix, from
380	[issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390)
381	"Hmc-Specifics messes up command line" (non-interactive-shaped terminal,
382	reporter on a Raspberry Pi): the maintainer's own prescribed and
383	reporter-confirmed fix is setting **`hmc.jline.enabled=false`** in
384	`HeadlessMC/config.properties` (also documented in the README's Termux
385	section — "Disable JLine, as we could not get it to work on Termux for now").
386	
387	Caveat from that same thread: the reporter *also* had the deprecated
388	`-commands` runtime flag active alongside hmc-specifics, which caused a
389	separate "every second command works" flakiness. Maintainer's explicit
390	guidance: never combine `-commands` with hmc-specifics — hmc-specifics alone
391	is the console surface. PATH 1 in this doc already avoids `-commands` — stay
392	that way.
393	
394	`headlessmc-jline/.../JLineProperties.java` exposes finer-grained flags no
395	one in the tracker has field-tested for this exact scenario but which read as
396	a more surgical fix than fully disabling JLine:
397	- `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` — auto-fall-back to JLine's
398	  dumb-terminal mode only when no real console/TTY is detected (exactly our
399	  "wrapper pipes stdio" case), keeping normal JLine behavior everywhere else.
400	- `hmc.jline.dumb=true` — force dumb mode unconditionally, the blunter
401	  version of the above.
402	
403	No mention anywhere in the org (issues, discussions, code) of node-pty or
404	ConPTY wrapping — that is **not** a known/documented HMC pattern. The
405	maintainer-endorsed route is purely the config-property route above; no
406	reason to stand up a pty shim.
407	
408	**Recommended order:** try `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first
409	(least invasive); fall back to `hmc.jline.enabled=false` (the confirmed fix
410	from #390) if commands still misbehave over the wrapper's plain pipe.

520	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.jline.VersionAgnosticJLineCommandLineReader.installAndReadAsyncAndAwaitException
521	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.SpecificsInitializer.readCommandLine
522	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.SpecificsInitializer.init
523	  at net.minecraft.class_310.handler$bck000$headlessmc$onInit   <- mixin into Minecraft's own constructor

is directly adjacent to chest A's own hitbox, zero buffer). Got genuinely wedged mid-test: jump-only
raw-control probe (with fresh look-wake, retried twice for good measure) read `moved:0` exact, real
full-wedge signature, not the jump-alone-false-read gotcha logged earlier this session (that one
needed forward+jump together to unstick — tried that too here, also 0). Ran the full self-rescue
ladder in order: (1) `/relog` — reconnected clean (`connected:true`) but wedge unchanged, identical
`moved:0` after a 10s+ settle wait (respecting the probe-timing gotcha); (2) `/trigger home` — this
one is new data: the server-side teleport was REAL and confirmed (`/status` position jumped from
11.49,89,55.3 all the way to the saved home 13.5,94,49.46, a genuine ~30-block displacement, not a
no-op) — but the CLIENT remained wedged afterward, `moved:0` again post-teleport. This matches
Grog's earlier-logged "full-wedge that survives BOTH the new home self-rescue AND relog" entry
almost exactly (same symptom: real server-side teleport, client desync persists) — this is now a
confirmed repeat of that pattern, not a one-off. Per that entry's resolution, the only known cure is
a hard runner process restart (teleport/relog alone don't resync client+server state). Escalated to
team-lead for the restart rather than continuing to poke at it. Suggest: this specific pinch (a
newly-dug 1-wide gap directly touching an existing furniture hitbox with zero buffer) may be an
easy way to REPRODUCE this wedge class on demand if anyone wants to debug the root desync — every
other full-wedge report this session was incidental/hard to reproduce, this one has a concrete
recipe (approach a chest-adjacent 1-wide doorway at a slight off-center angle and push forward).

## [shipped] Tunnel Job 1 complete — y49 access tunnel x40→28 bored, exposes cluster-2 iron, no breach — BariBrute, 2026-09-01 14:48
Bored the pivot-proving tunnel per team-lead's brief. Started at (44,49,60) per brief but the
facing field-test (below) drifted the working start to x=40 before the real dig kicked off, so
depth was cut from the specified `d:16` to `d:12` to preserve the intended endpoint — final line
ran clean **x=40→28, y=49-50 (h:2,w:1), z=60**, straight through the cluster-2 iron band
(38-39,y47-48,z59-60). Log evidence: composite goal `GoalComposite[16x GoalBreak...]` shrank
monotonically over ~5.5 min (BetterBlockPos progression 40→39→37→35→34→done), ended clean with
"Done building" then `#eta`→"No process in control" (genuine finish, not a self-cancel-on-stall).
No lava/water/fall/damage/exception lines anywhere in the dig window. **Breach check**: could not
block-scan the final cavity via neighbor-eval (both Zug and UngaBunga were busy on their own
driver's tasks the whole window — genuine contention, not a bug) — reporting UNCONFIRMED rather
than guessing; no hazard indicators in the log either way. Ore was deliberately left unmined per
brief (harvest crew's job).

**FACING field-verify (deliverable)**: `#tunnel` digs in whatever direction Baritone is currently
facing — there is no dedicated aim/look/turn chat command, and the wrapper's `/console` whitelist
(`#eta #proc #goal #version #pause #resume`) doesn't expose one either. Tested empirically: a
short ~1-block `#goto` hop west did NOT reliably set yaw toward west (ended ~1.8°, not ~90°) —
falsifies the naive "any short goto sets facing" assumption. A longer ~4-block `#goto` hop DID
converge yaw toward the travel direction (179.85°→1.8°→75.6° across successive tests), though not
exactly precise. **Working recipe: fire a `#goto` several blocks (4+) in the intended tunnel
direction before `#tunnel`, not a 1-block nudge.**

Two more quirks found riding along on this job:
1. **Composite-goal planning delay reads as a false stall.** Right after issuing `#tunnel` with a
   large footprint, `#eta` returns `NaN` and position telemetry sits frozen for 60-120s while
   Baritone computes the full `GoalComposite[...]` node list — this is real compute time, not a
   stuck bot. Confirmed via block-state ground-truth (open cavern, solid iron floor, no physical
   obstruction) plus a full log-tail read (found the composite had just finished building). Don't
   `/stop` on this signature alone — check the log for "Finished finding a path" before assuming
   stuck.
2. **`positionSource: "goal-poll"` reports the ACTIVE GOAL TARGET, not the bot's real position.**
   Caught red-handed on the return `/goto {"x":20,"y":90,"z":60}`: `/status` showed
   `position:{x:20,y:90,z:60}` **the instant the goto was issued**, 90+ seconds before the bot
   could plausibly have covered that distance (41 y-levels + 13 x-blocks). Root cause: goal-poll
   is parsing the `Goal: GoalBlock{x=20,y=90,z=60}` chat echo as if it were a position report, not
   an actual position sample. This makes `/status`'s `position` field **completely untrustworthy
   whenever any goal is active** (goto/mine/tunnel) — it'll show the destination, not progress,
   from tick one. Combined with the earlier-logged "position sometimes never updates during a
   whole task" entry, the real fix recommendation is the same: `/status` needs a genuine
   entity-position poll (e.g. periodic bare `#pos`-equivalent if one exists, or parsing movement
   packets) decoupled from whatever `#goal`/`#eta` happen to print.

**Return leg + the "silent arrival" pattern**: the return `/goto` self-cleared to "No process in
control" (confirmed via both `#eta` and `#proc`) ~2min7s after issue, with ZERO intermediate chat
lines (no replan spam, no "Finished finding a path", no arrival announcement) — worrying at first
glance given the earlier session's identical-looking silent self-cancel-on-ascend-refusal failure
(see below). Disambiguated by re-issuing the same `/goto`: it produced NO "Starting to search for
path from BetterBlockPos{...}" line at all before immediately going idle again — Baritone only
skips path search when already standing in the goal cell. Two goes at this exact same clean
signature = confident read that the goto genuinely arrived, just never announced it (consistent
with this session's standing "near-zero completion telemetry" theme). Ground-truth neighbor-eval
was unavailable both times (Zug/UngaBunga both busy on their own tasks) — noting the confirmation
method used instead (re-issue-and-check-for-skipped-pathsearch) as a new trick worth keeping
alongside the `#eta` probe for exactly this ambiguous-silence situation.

**Real anomaly hit mid-return**: the FIRST attempt at the return `/goto {"x":20,"y":90,"z":60}`
(fired right after tunnel completion, from (33,49,60)) found a full 30384-node path fine but then
hit 8x "Too far to the side to safely sprint ascend" / "Skipping traverse to straight ascend" and
silently self-cancelled without ever taking a single step (position never left x=33) — same
failure signature as this session's very first `/goto` anomaly (already logged above). Fix that
worked: `/stop` to clear the stale task, then a plain retry of the identical `/goto` — second
attempt replanned differently and completed clean. Two-for-two now on "stop + blind retry" as the
correct response to this specific silent-ascend-refusal pattern — worth promoting from "anomaly
response" to "standard first move" when a fresh goto shows repeated ascend-refusal spam then goes
quiet with zero position change.

**legitMine live-flip blocker (chief ruling 2026-09-01)**: attempted `POST /console
{"cmd":"#set legitMine false"}` per team-lead's instruction to flip it live mid-session — rejected
outright: `{"error":"command not whitelisted","allowed":["#eta","#proc","#goal","#version",
"#pause","#resume"]}`. The wrapper's `/console` whitelist does not include `#set` at all, so the
"works mid-session" assumption doesn't hold through the documented HTTP API as-is — would need
either a wrapper code change (extends the whitelist, a safety-relevant surface) or a full relaunch
to take effect, neither attempted mid-tunnel-job. Applied the PERSISTENT half only: settings.txt
template in `baritone-runner.mjs` and `cave/BARITONE.md` part 5a both updated
(`legitMine true`→`false`), all other safety settings untouched. Low urgency noted: `legitMine`
only gates `#mine`'s visibility-based targeting, not `#tunnel`'s deterministic dig-in-place
behavior, so it had zero effect on this job either way. Live effect deferred to BariBrute's next
natural relaunch.

while true; do
  s=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3302/status)
  task=$(echo "$s" | grep -o '"task":[^,}]*\|"task":{[^}]*}')

  if echo "$aborted" | grep -q 'nogo'; then
    echo "ALERT NOGO ABORT — bot got stopped/redirected by watchdog"
    break
  fi
  if echo "$task" | grep -q '"task":null'; then
    echo "TERMINAL task cleared — arrived or self-cancelled, check position via neighbor eval"
    break
  fi
  if [ "$line" = "$prevline" ]; then
    samecount=$((samecount+1))
  else
    samecount=0

  prevline="$line"
  if [ "$samecount" -ge 3 ] && echo "$line" | grep -qiE 'ascend|too far to the side'; then
    echo "ALERT STALL-SIGNATURE ascend-refusal repeated $samecount times, task not progressing — candidate for stop+retry"
    break
  fi
  sleep 20
done

  sleep 40
  elapsed=$((elapsed+40))
done
